references.text: The woman originally came to the well to draw water with her jar ([ref:Joh 4:7|John 4:7]). Now she leaves her jar behind – meeting Jesus has completely changed her priorities.
The woman went into the town and said to the people, 'Come, see a man who told me everything I have done!' ([ref:Joh 4:29|John 4:29]). This verse expands on what she said to the people in the town.
The woman's testimony led many Samaritans to believe in Jesus ([ref:Joh 4:39|John 4:39]), showing the fruit of her leaving her jar and going into the town.

When Jesus called his disciples Simon and Andrew, they immediately left their nets and followed him ([ref:Mark 1:18|Mark 1:18]). In a similar way, the Samaritan woman left her water jar – both actions symbolize laying aside one's daily work to follow Jesus' call.

Simon and Andrew left their nets, and James and John left the boat and their father to follow Jesus ([ref:Matt 4:20-22|Matthew 4:20-22]). Leaving behind one's tools and daily labor is a recurring pattern when people encounter Jesus.

Andrew found his brother Simon and brought him to Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:40-42|John 1:40-42]). Just as Andrew went and told others after meeting Jesus, the Samaritan woman did the same by going into the town and telling people about him.

Philip found Nathanael and invited him to 'come and see' Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:45-46|John 1:45-46]). The woman's response – going and telling others about Jesus – follows the same pattern of personal testimony that leads others to Christ.

The disciples left everything and followed Jesus ([ref:Luk 5:11|Luke 5:11]). That the woman left her water jar symbolizes a similar response – letting go of earthly things to share the message about Jesus.
